This effectively reduces the validation to a single small split, raising overfitting concerns. AUC alone does not capture the clinical operating point — sensitivity and specificity at clinically meaningful thresholds should drive the evaluation.
scenarios.ood_provenance: eLife reviewed preprint (open public reviews). Paper: 'Predictive modeling of hematoma expansion from non-contrast CT in spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage' (2025). Public Reviewer 1 raised small-sample, single-split and AUC-alone concerns.

_provenance.cp_relabel_v4_ood: REPLACED v?=[CP-040] -> [CP-024,CP-020]. CP-024 (insufficient sample size; sample_size_gate) is the canonical match for 'n=170 training + 170 external test, overfitting risk'. CP-020 (clinically critical metric omitted; clinical_metrics_gate; tag missing_sensitivity_specificity) matches 'AUC alone insufficient; sens/spec at clinically meaningful thresholds'. Original CP-040 (inconsistent cohort numbers) misses.

scenarios.description: eLife reviewed preprint on NMR metabolomics + ML for predicting progression from prediabetes to type-2 diabetes in UK Biobank. Reviewer 1 questions why exactly the top-20 metabolites were retained (arbitrary), asks for explicit hyperparameter search ranges for the random survival forest, notes the NMR platform is lipid-biased, and limits generalizability to a predominantly White cohort with no external validation.
scenarios.query_text: Why retain exactly the top 20 metabolites rather than apply a more principled threshold? The hyperparameter search space for the random survival forest is not laid out, and the NMR platform used in UK Biobank is biased toward lipid species, which risks measurement-platform bias in the selected signature. The cohort is also predominantly White and there is no external validation, which limits generalizability beyond UK Biobank.
scenarios.ood_provenance: eLife reviewed preprint (open public reviews). Paper: 'Nuclear magnetic resonance-based metabolomics with machine learning for predicting progression from prediabetes to diabetes' (2024-2025). Public Reviewer 1 raised feature-count, hyperparameter-search, NMR-platform-bias, and generalizability concerns.

_provenance.cp_relabel_v4_ood: REFINED replacement. CP-019 (feature selection stability/method; feature_engineering_audit_gate; tag feature_count_arbitrary loosely; alternative_feature_selection_methods) matches 'why top-20 metabolites? hyperparameter search undefined'. CP-033 (underrepresented subgroup; fairness_equity_gate; tags ancestry_diversity, race_underrepresentation) matches 'predominantly White cohort'. CP-008 (missing external validation) matches 'no external validation'. Original CP-018 is too narrow.

scenarios.description: Multimodal LLM (SkinGPT-4) for dermatological diagnosis trained and evaluated on imagery that under-represents Fitzpatrick IV-VI skin, so reported diagnostic performance does not characterize how the model behaves on darker skin tones.
scenarios.query_text: How well does the training corpus actually represent darker skin (Fitzpatrick IV-VI)? Skin of color is chronically under-represented in dermatology image datasets, and without a per-Fitzpatrick breakdown of sensitivity and specificity we cannot tell whether the headline accuracy holds for patients with deeply pigmented skin or whether the model would systematically miss disease in that group.

scenarios.description: Dermatology AI evaluated on a real-world supplementary case set whose patient demographics are not reported and whose photos visibly skew to one skin color, leaving any fairness gap invisible in the evaluation.
scenarios.query_text: The validation set is presented without any demographic description of the patients, and on inspection the supplementary cases are dominated by one skin color. Because the evaluation itself is not stratified by skin tone or any protected attribute, any disparate performance the model has across patient groups is simply not measured, which is a serious omission for a diagnostic tool.

scenarios.description: Clinical-notes NLP model for chemotherapy toxicity extraction shows performance variability across ethnicities, but the discussion never engages with the disparity, offers no mechanistic hypotheses, and proposes no fairness mitigation.
scenarios.query_text: Performance differences across ethnic groups are visible in the results but the discussion does not engage with them. Authors should explicitly acknowledge the subgroup disparities, hypothesize why they arise (training-data composition, label noise, language differences in notes), and propose concrete mitigation such as targeted fine-tuning, reweighting, or fairness-aware objectives.

scenarios.description: Vision-transformer model for recurrent HCC treatment decisions reports no sex/gender breakdown of cohort or performance, in direct violation of the SAGER guidelines flagged in the journal's review instructions.
scenarios.query_text: The manuscript provides no sex/gender breakdown of the cohort and no sex-stratified performance, which means it does not satisfy the SAGER guidelines that the journal explicitly asks reviewers to enforce. For a treatment-decision model, the absence of sex-specific characterization is not just a reporting gap, it actively hides any sex-related disparity in the model's recommendations.

scenarios.description: Baseline-ECG model predicting chemotherapy-induced cardiotoxicity reports pooled performance only, despite well-known sex differences in cardiovascular outcomes and ECG morphology.
scenarios.query_text: Cardiovascular disease and baseline ECG features differ substantially between men and women, yet the evaluation reports a single pooled performance for both models. A sex-stratified analysis of discrimination and calibration is the minimum needed to show the predictor is not silently worse for one sex, and should be added before any clinical-use claim.

scenarios.description: Cross-ancestry polygenic risk score method is benchmarked only on East Asian and European samples, with no evaluation on African-ancestry cohorts where PRS transferability is known to be substantially worse.
scenarios.query_text: The evaluation is confined to East Asian and European ancestry samples. African-ancestry transferability of polygenic scores is consistently the hardest case in the literature, and a method that claims cross-ancestry portability needs to be tested on AFR cohorts before any equity-relevant claim can be made. Limiting validation to two ancestries effectively bakes in the genomic-medicine disparity the field is supposed to be closing.

scenarios.description: Genetic Progression Score for RA/SLE that combines EHR with GWAS summary statistics, but reports performance only in the European-ancestry subset of BioVU and All of Us, with non-European subsets too small to evaluate.
scenarios.query_text: Performance is only reported on the European-ancestry slice of BioVU and All of Us; the non-European subsets are too small for any fairness or transferability statement. For a score being positioned as a clinical screening tool, the cross-ancestry portability question must be answered, not silently sidestepped by a sample-size argument.

scenarios.description: T2D risk model in a Taiwan Biobank cohort applies its early-detection analysis only to women aged 59 and above without justifying either the sex restriction or the age threshold, and does not test generalizability to men.
scenarios.query_text: The early-detection analysis is restricted to women aged 59 and older, but no biological, clinical, or statistical rationale is given for either the sex restriction or the age cutoff. Either justify the subgroup choice from prior literature on T2D incidence, or extend the analysis to men and to younger strata and report whether the predictor generalizes outside the chosen window.

scenarios.description: Multiethnic skin-cancer XGBoost model where ancestry labels drive the analysis, but the method for assigning ancestry (self-report vs genotype PCA), the definition of the Admixed group, and the exclusion of Native American ancestry are all unexplained.
scenarios.query_text: How were patients assigned to ancestry groups: self-reported race, genotype PCA, or some hybrid, and how much do those two labels agree in this cohort? How exactly is the Admixed category defined, and why is Native American ancestry not represented? Without these definitions the multiethnic framing is not auditable, and any per-group performance claim could be an artifact of the labelling scheme.

scenarios.description: Plasma-proteomics classifier of pediatric TB versus non-TB respiratory disease reports no subgroup analyses by age under 2, sex, HIV status, or nutritional status, despite large HIV and malnutrition imbalance between TB cases and controls.
scenarios.query_text: There is substantial imbalance in HIV status and nutritional status between the TB and Unlikely-TB groups, and the youngest children (under 2) are a clinically distinct subgroup. No stratified performance by age band, sex, HIV, or nutritional status is provided, which means the proteomic signature could be tracking comorbidity prevalence rather than TB biology, with predictable equity consequences in deployment.

scenarios.description: Tumor-infiltrating TCR-repertoire study where each subject yields only ~10 unique clonotypes, far below literature norms; suggests sampling bias or a sequencing/quantification artifact in the wet-lab pipeline, and raw reads are not shared.
scenarios.query_text: The median number of distinct TCR sequences recovered per subject is around ten, which is an order of magnitude below what comparable repertoire studies report. This very likely reflects either a sampling problem or a methodological artifact in how clonotypes were called, and the authors do not give a precise clonotype definition or release the underlying sequencing reads for the sixteen subjects.

scenarios.description: Colorectal cancer integrated polygenic + lifestyle risk score reported only via hazard ratios, AUC and Kaplan-Meier curves, lacking sensitivity/specificity/PPV at usable thresholds, decision curve analysis, and variance-explained for the polygenic score.
scenarios.query_text: Reported model statistics are restricted to effect sizes, AUC, and Kaplan-Meier / log-rank tests. For a score that is being positioned as clinically useful, the authors should also report sensitivity, specificity, and PPV at proposed thresholds, perform a decision curve analysis, and quantify how much variance of the outcome the polygenic component actually explains.

scenarios.description: Stroke outcome ML model bootstraps only inside the inner CV loop; the headline train/test partition is never resampled, leaving the reported AUC, accuracy and specificity exposed to a lucky-split bias with no real CIs.
scenarios.query_text: Bootstrapping is applied only within the cross-validation procedure, while the train/test split itself is never repeated. That leaves substantial room for cherry-picking a favorable partition, and the reported AUC, accuracy, and specificity have no proper confidence intervals built around the actual evaluation that the paper is selling.

scenarios.description: NSCLC immunotherapy adaptation study where the original five proposed methods failed external validation, then three new methods were added post hoc; only one of the new methods reaches borderline p-values without correction for the eight comparisons.
scenarios.query_text: All five originally proposed methods failed on the two validation cohorts, and three additional methods were introduced afterwards without flagging this clearly. Only one of those new methods reaches significance, with p-values of 0.016 and 0.0076. Since eight methods have now been screened against the same validation cohorts, the authors must apply some form of multiplicity correction before claiming the new method is validated.

scenarios.description: PRStuning polygenic risk score paper compares only against custom variants, but summary statistics for T2D, CAD and IBD are publicly available; the authors should benchmark against an established LDpred2 baseline including runtime.
scenarios.query_text: Public GWAS summary statistics for T2D, CAD, and IBD are readily available, so a head-to-head comparison against a traditional LDpred2 baseline on UK Biobank is straightforward. The authors should add such a comparison, reporting both AUC and runtime, before claiming that PRStuning offers a practical advantage.

scenarios.description: NetBio immunotherapy-response classifier reports modest AUROCs on a small, imbalanced responder/non-responder cohort, with no AUPRC, no class distribution, and no confusion tables to expose how optimistic AUROC is here.
scenarios.query_text: The NetBio improvements over PD1 / PD-L1 features look real but the absolute AUROC values are still modest. With a small cohort and an unstated class balance between responders and non-responders, AUROC can be optimistic. Precision-Recall curves annotated with class prevalence and confusion tables would be needed to honestly judge performance.

scenarios.description: Pathology gigapixel deep-learning model for lymph node metastasis presented without adherence to MI-CLAIM, TRIPOD-ML or any other EQUATOR reporting guideline, leaving methods underspecified for systematic appraisal.
scenarios.query_text: The manuscript does not appear to follow any of the established reporting guidelines for clinical machine learning, such as MI-CLAIM or TRIPOD-ML on the EQUATOR network. Adopting one of these checklists would let readers and reviewers systematically verify the methods and avoid having to reconstruct missing details by hand.

scenarios.description: DILImap toxicogenomics classifier with a claimed 100% specificity but no description of how train/validation sets were built, whether the CV operated on all drugs or only the training subset, or what was done to control compound-level leakage.
scenarios.query_text: It is not stated whether cross-validation was run over the entire DILImap or only over the training subset, and no description is given of how the train/validation partitions were constructed or how compound-level leakage was prevented. Given the headline claim of 100% specificity, this lack of split protocol is a significant credibility issue.

scenarios.description: Multimodal LLM dermatology assistant (SkinGPT-4) evaluated without reporting patient demographics, and the supplementary real-life examples mostly show a single skin tone, so Fitzpatrick subgroup performance and bias are entirely unmeasured.
scenarios.query_text: No patient demographics are provided for the validation cohort, and the real-life cases in the supplement are dominated by one skin tone. As a result, any bias of the model across Fitzpatrick skin types is invisible from this evaluation, which is a serious weakness for a dermatology tool.

scenarios.description: Type-2 diabetes precision phenotyping paper uses a variational autoencoder without clarifying whether it serves as representation learner, feature selector or denoiser, and without comparing against simpler baselines such as a vanilla AE, PCA or supervised selection.
scenarios.query_text: It is never clearly stated whether the variational autoencoder is used for representation learning, feature selection, denoising, or some combination, nor why it is preferred over a vanilla autoencoder, PCA, or a directly supervised selector. The text claims the latent space is informative and the input is denoised, but no comparative experiments back this up.

scenarios.description: Antimicrobial resistance GNN paper where the documented pipeline requires a precomputed adjacency matrix rather than raw genomic assemblies, but the repo lacks any instructions for going from sequencing data to model input, blocking reproduction.
scenarios.query_text: The figures suggest the model takes unitigs, SNPs, and FCGR-derived features, but the methods and demo data actually expect a precomputed adjacency matrix as input. There are no instructions in the repository for training AMR-GNN end-to-end or for converting raw sequencing data into the required graph representation, which prevents independent reuse.

scenarios.description: Immunotherapy-response NetBio paper applies RECIST only to an unspecified subset of patients and uses dataset-provided responder labels for the rest, leaving the operational definition of the outcome inconsistent across the training data.
scenarios.query_text: Defining responders versus non-responders is central to this study, yet the methods only say that RECIST criteria were applied to some patients and that for the rest the labels supplied by the source datasets were reused. How many patients fall into each category, and what exact rules did the upstream datasets use? Without that, the ground truth is heterogeneous in an undocumented way.

scenarios.description: COVID severity model derived from chest CT plus clinical variables, where the time from admission to critical outcome is the target, but the timing of each CT relative to disease course is not recorded, opening a clear lead-time / look-ahead bias.
scenarios.query_text: The outcome is measured as time from admission to critical severity or death, but the manuscript never says when during the hospital course each chest CT was acquired. If scans were taken at different stages of illness, then any apparent prognostic signal could simply reflect when the imaging happened to be done rather than what it shows, which is a classic lead-time bias.

scenarios.description: Real-time COVID mortality EHR model communicates output as a 0-100 percentile rank rather than an absolute probability, which obscures calibration and makes thresholding for clinical action awkward.
scenarios.query_text: Why is mortality risk reported on a 0-100 percentile scale rather than as an absolute probability? Percentile ranks shift with the underlying population and are very hard for clinicians to translate into actions. An absolute probability with calibration plots would be far easier to interpret and act on.

scenarios.description: Explainable EHR model predicting three acute outcomes with prevalences of 2.44%, 0.75% and 1.68%, where no description is given of class-imbalance handling such as loss weighting, resampling, or threshold tuning.
scenarios.query_text: The three target outcomes occur in only 2.44%, 0.75%, and 1.68% of patients. The methods should state whether any imbalance-mitigation techniques were used during training (loss weighting, oversampling, undersampling, focal loss, threshold tuning), since with that level of class imbalance the choice matters a great deal for both training behavior and reported metrics.

scenarios.description: Alzheimer's brain-scan deep-learning framework where different figures draw on different unspecified subsets of the cohort, with no per-figure sample sizes and no clearly described inclusion or diagnostic criteria.
scenarios.query_text: Different figures in the paper appear to use different subsets of the cohort, but neither the legends nor the methods say which subset is used in which analysis or how many subjects are involved each time. A brief per-figure description of the included subset, sample size, and underlying inclusion / diagnostic criteria would substantially improve transparency.

scenarios.description: Pediatric ECG deep-learning model for congenital heart disease lacks a baseline characteristics table and never reports performance stratified by patient age, sex, or heart rate.
scenarios.query_text: Model accuracy should be reported stratified by patient age, sex, and resting heart rate, since each of these is known to affect pediatric ECG morphology. The paper also lacks a baseline characteristics table for the cohort, which makes it hard to assess representativeness or check for confounding.

scenarios.description: ICU acuity state-space model whose public GitHub repository omits software/hardware requirements, dependency pins, and any explanation of how hyperparameters were chosen (search procedure vs. ad-hoc tuning).
scenarios.query_text: The GitHub repository for this work does not list the required software and hardware, omits dependency versions, and gives no description of how the reported hyperparameters were arrived at (grid search, Bayesian optimization, hand-tuning, or otherwise). All three are basic prerequisites for an independent group to rerun the experiments.

scenarios.description: Twelve-lead ECG deep network where the existing evaluation does not enforce a patient-grouped split or a chronological train/val/test ordering; reviewer asks for both, plus inter-rater reliability against humans.
scenarios.query_text: Please add an experiment with a 90/5/5 train/validation/test split in which all traces from the same individual are kept in the same fold, and a second experiment with a strictly chronological split (oldest 90% for training, next 5% for validation, newest 5% for test) to simulate prospective deployment. The comparison against human readers on the final test set should also report inter-rater reliability.

scenarios.description: Chemotherapy cardiotoxicity AI-EF model evaluation that draws from the same multi-center pool (BWH, MGH, UCSF, Keio) used in the model's original derivation paper, with no explicit patient-level check ruling out overlap with the previous training and validation cohorts.
scenarios.query_text: The AI-EF model was originally derived from data at BWH, MGH, UCSF, and Keio, and the current evaluation cohort appears to be drawn from the same institutions. Did the authors explicitly verify at the patient level that none of the subjects in this evaluation appeared in the original training or validation sets? Without that check, the reported performance could be inflated by overlap with the pretraining data.

scenarios.description: Type-2 diabetes VAE classifier reported without hyperparameter search spaces, selection criteria, nested CV structure, or fold definitions, and it is unclear which results use the full feature set versus the ten 'VAE-selected' features.
scenarios.query_text: Essential methodological details are missing: the hyperparameter search spaces and selection criteria are not described, the nested CV structure and fold definitions are absent, and no explicit safeguards against leakage between feature selection and evaluation are documented. It is also unclear in which experiments the model uses the full feature set versus only the ten VAE-selected features.

scenarios.description: Vision transformer for recurrent HCC whose title claims the model 'optimizes curative-intent treatment selection', but the actual modeling target is OS/PFS prognostication; no counterfactual analysis links the score to treatment-choice benefit.
scenarios.query_text: The algorithm predicts overall and progression-free survival, which is prognostication, not a treatment-selection decision. To actually inform whether a patient should receive local therapy versus systemic treatment or TACE / TARE you would need a counterfactual analysis comparing outcomes under each option. As it stands the title overclaims what the model can support.

scenarios.description: Drug-induced liver injury model trained on 24-hour RNA-seq from sandwich-cultured 2D primary hepatocytes; in-vitro de-differentiation and short exposure window create a systematic gap with chronic/idiosyncratic in-vivo DILI.
scenarios.query_text: Training relies on 24-hour RNA-seq from sandwich-cultured primary human hepatocytes. It is well documented that 2D hepatocyte culture causes substantial de-differentiation of the transcriptome, and a single-day exposure cannot capture idiosyncratic toxicities that typically emerge over weeks to months. The authors should at minimum discuss how this training-data selection might bias the mechanistic DILI predictions.

scenarios.description: Early-stage NSCLC ctDNA recurrence model pools adenocarcinoma and squamous patients; survival baselines and ctDNA detection rates differ by subtype, but no subtype-stratified analyses are reported.
scenarios.query_text: The analysis pools early-stage lung adenocarcinoma and squamous-cell carcinoma patients, even though these subtypes have noticeably different baseline recurrence and survival profiles and the paper itself notes that adenocarcinoma tumors shed ctDNA at a lower rate. Without subtype-stratified survival analyses, the headline results are confounded by tumor type.

scenarios.description: COVID severity classifier where higher severity scores in patients admitted more than four days after symptom onset are interpreted as a delayed-admission effect, but the pattern is consistent with lead-time bias and is not adjusted for days since symptom onset.
scenarios.query_text: Patients admitted more than four days after symptom onset show higher severity scores, but COVID severity is known to rise naturally until around day ten of illness, so this almost certainly reflects lead-time bias rather than a true effect of delayed admission. The risk score and the associated analyses should be adjusted for days since symptom onset, and the role of lead-time bias should be explicitly discussed.

scenarios.description: CP-002 future-info leakage + CP-008 no external validation (paper PR-001: musculoskeletal / 5-year osteoarthritis risk prediction)
scenarios.query_text: The models look forward across the 5-year follow-up window and condition on covariates (e.g. NSAID exposure) that only become observable after baseline — so this is closer to a retrospective characterisation than a prospective predictor. Compounding that, what the authors call external validation is just a held-out slice of the same UK Biobank cohort; there is no independent dataset, which makes the headline performance claims hard to take at face value.

scenarios.description: CP-015 imputation/missingness leakage + CP-026 AUC-only evaluation lacking calibration/DCA (paper PR-003: infectious_disease / COVID-19 in-hospital mortality prediction)
scenarios.query_text: Was the validation cohort imputed using parameters fitted on the development cohort? Missing-data fractions per feature are not reported and that opens the door to information bleeding across the split. On top of that, the paper leans entirely on AUC; there is no calibration curve and no decision-curve analysis, which together makes it impossible to judge whether the biomarker actually buys anything clinically over the existing COVID-19 mortality scores.

scenarios.description: CP-022 confounding by stage/incremental value + CP-011 reproducibility/methods detail missing (paper PR-005: oncology / Gastric cancer prognosis and immunotherapy response prediction from CT images)
scenarios.query_text: How do we know the deep-learning signature is doing anything beyond proxying tumour size and stage, which are themselves dominant prognostic factors? The paper does not show incremental value over a stage-adjusted baseline. Separately, the methods section is too thin for anyone to actually reproduce the pipeline — neither the CT pre-processing choices nor the data splits are specified at the level needed.

scenarios.description: CP-002 spectrum/prevalence bias + CP-022 weak explainability of imaging model (paper PR-007: oncology / Ovarian cancer diagnosis from ultrasound + clinical variables)
scenarios.query_text: Roughly half of the training masses are malignant, which is wildly out of line with community prevalence (under 5%); the resulting spectrum bias likely inflates every operating-point metric reported here. And the explanation of what the network is actually attending to in the ultrasound is hand-wavy — Grad-CAM heatmaps with a sentence about 'highlighting important regions' is not interpretability, and gives clinicians no way to sanity-check predictions on the hard cases.

scenarios.description: CP-003 mislabelled prospective claim + CP-006 rare-event PPV / AUC overoptimism (paper PR-009: critical_care / ICU patient acuity and life-sustaining therapy prediction (4-hour horizon))
scenarios.query_text: The abstract describes the 2021-2023 evaluation as prospective, but Mamba did not exist until 2023, so this was clearly retrospective scoring on historical data; the framing needs to be corrected. Independently, for rare ICU events AUC is a poor stand-alone metric — PPV will be low and the practical clinician-facing performance unclear, so a clinician-adjudication subset and PPV/calibration reporting are needed before any clinical-utility claim.

scenarios.description: CP-011 irreproducible methods (rate calc) + CP-001 post-hoc outcome selection (paper PR-013: neurology / ALS disease progression tracking and severity prediction from wearable accelerometers)
scenarios.query_text: I cannot tell from the methods how the rate of decline was actually computed — no longitudinal model is reported, and a per-patient regression with no shrinkage would behave very differently from a mixed model. That ambiguity becomes more serious because the primary outcome (the limb with the fastest progression) appears to be picked after the fact; in a trial setting that endpoint would have to be prespecified, otherwise the apparent sensitivity is inflated by selection.

scenarios.description: CP-014 overparameterised feature/sample ratio + CP-001 training-set performance reported as result (paper PR-016: oncology / Breast cancer survival prediction from MRI radiomics + genomic features)
scenarios.query_text: The radiogenomic model is heavily overparameterised — well over a hundred features against under a hundred cases — so the reported survival signal could plausibly be fit-to-noise. That suspicion is reinforced by Figures 4d and 7d, which look like training-set curves; if so they should not be presented as model performance at all, and the held-out estimates need to be the headline numbers.

scenarios.description: CP-001 overfitting / parameter selection + CP-029 European-only ancestry generalisability (paper PR-018: genomics / PRS parameter tuning without external validation data (PRStuning method))
scenarios.query_text: For both C+T and LDpred the chosen-parameter AUCs sit suspiciously close to where you'd expect overfitting to peak — is this convergence or is the tuning procedure selecting on noise? On top of that, the entire framework was developed and tuned on European-ancestry summary statistics, so any claim of method-generality is overstated until non-European cohorts are included.

scenarios.description: CP-010 potential clinical harm from overtreatment + CP-021 invalid DCA assumptions (paper PR-020: oncology / Thyroid cancer lateral lymph node metastasis prediction from multimodal data)
scenarios.query_text: Detecting microscopic lateral lymph-node metastases with AI is not unambiguously beneficial — for many of these patients dissection will not change outcomes and will add morbidity, so the model could drive overtreatment. The decision-curve analysis used to justify clinical utility silently assumes every true-positive is a net win, which is exactly the assumption that breaks here; the DCA as presented is misleading.

scenarios.description: CP-002 missing prediction horizon (diagnosis vs future risk) + CP-015 missing-data not MNAR-handled (paper PR-024: oncology / Early cancer diagnosis prediction for 15 cancer types from primary care EHR)
scenarios.query_text: Nowhere can I find the time horizon over which the model is supposed to predict — are we forecasting an imminent diagnosis or longer-term risk? Without this the very high AUCs may just reflect already-symptomatic disease. The missingness analysis also shows the data are not MCAR, but the imputation strategy does not handle MNAR and the per-variable missing counts and a bias analysis are not reported.

scenarios.description: scRNA-seq cell-type deconvolution affecting downstream differential expression — single-cell omics scope.
scenarios.query_text: We deconvolved bulk-tumor expression with CIBERSORTx using a scRNA-seq reference, then ran DESeq2 on the inferred cell-type fractions. Reviewer worries the deconvolution residuals correlate with library size and inflate DEG calls. How should we validate the deconvolution-to-DEG pipeline?

scenarios.description: GWAS population-stratification confounding via principal components — population-genetics omics scope.
scenarios.query_text: Our GWAS of LDL-C in a multi-ancestry UK Biobank subset shows lambda_GC = 1.18 even after 10 PCs. Should we add mixed-model BOLT-LMM, regress more PCs, or restrict to a single-ancestry stratum? Concerned about residual population stratification inflating hits.

scenarios.description: TCGA bulk-RNA batch correction with ComBat removing real biology — bulk-omics scope.
scenarios.query_text: We merged TCGA-BRCA and METABRIC microarray expression with ComBat to train a subtype classifier. Reviewer claims ComBat over-correction collapsed the basal-vs-luminal axis. Is there a recommended diagnostic to detect biology-leakage into the batch term?

scenarios.description: U-Net segmentation Dice degrades under scanner slice-thickness mismatch — medical-imaging segmentation scope.
scenarios.query_text: Our 3D U-Net for pancreas segmentation reaches Dice 0.81 on the in-house 1.5mm CT cohort but drops to 0.64 on an external 5mm cohort. We suspect anisotropic-spacing drift. Should we add MONAI's Spacingd resampling or train multi-resolution heads?

scenarios.description: Chest X-ray DL classifier learning hospital-logo / device tokens — imaging-classification shortcut scope.
scenarios.query_text: A DenseNet-121 trained on CheXpert+MIMIC-CXR achieves AUROC 0.93 for pneumothorax, but Grad-CAM heatmaps light up on chest-drain pixels and the laterality marker. Is there a standard saliency-disagreement protocol to quantify shortcut reliance before deployment?

scenarios.description: Inter-subject MRI registration introducing template bias in VBM — neuroimaging-registration scope.
scenarios.query_text: Voxel-based morphometry on a 600-subject T1w MRI cohort uses SPM12 DARTEL to a study-specific template. Reviewer worries case/control imbalance biases the template toward controls and shrinks reported gray-matter differences. How do we audit registration-induced bias?

scenarios.description: BERT fine-tuned on radiology reports overfits to template phrasing — clinical-NLP scope.
scenarios.query_text: We fine-tuned ClinicalBERT to flag incidental pulmonary nodules from free-text CT reports. F1 on the source institution is 0.91 but drops to 0.62 at an external site that uses a different dictation template. Are there established de-templatization or attention-masking strategies?

scenarios.description: LLM extraction from clinical notes leaks gold-label phrases via prompt — clinical-NLP / generative scope.
scenarios.query_text: We use GPT-class zero-shot prompting to extract sepsis-onset timestamps from MIMIC-IV discharge summaries. The prompt happens to include the phrase "first documented sepsis-3 criteria," which appears verbatim in many notes. Is this a recognized form of prompt-induced label leakage in clinical NLP?

scenarios.description: Cox proportional-hazards assumption violated for 5-year survival — survival-analysis scope.
scenarios.query_text: Our Cox PH model for 5-year overall survival in resected NSCLC shows Schoenfeld-residual p < 0.01 for the stage covariate, suggesting non-proportional hazards. Should we switch to time-varying coefficients, stratify on stage, or use a flexible-parametric Royston-Parmar model?

scenarios.description: Competing-risks bias when using Kaplan-Meier instead of Fine-Gray — survival/competing-risks scope.
scenarios.query_text: We reported cumulative incidence of cardiovascular death in a CKD cohort using 1 - Kaplan-Meier, treating non-CV death as censoring. A reviewer insists this overestimates CIF and we should use the Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard. How serious is this in practice for a 10-year horizon?

scenarios.description: Surface uses 'input features' and 'calibration' vocab; real intent is a clinical pharmacology question about aspirin's effect on platelet counts.
scenarios.query_text: I notice platelet count is one of the input features feeding the calibration step. How does chronic low-dose aspirin use affect platelet counts in a cohort like this, and should the authors stratify the calibration curve by antiplatelet status?

scenarios.description: Mentions 'feature engineering' and 'external validation' but the real question is a clinical one about which eGFR equation to use for creatinine-based kidney function.
scenarios.query_text: The feature engineering pipeline derives eGFR from serum creatinine before external validation. In a multi-ethnic cohort, would the CKD-EPI 2021 race-free equation give meaningfully different kidney function values than MDRD, and which is clinically more defensible here?

scenarios.description: Uses 'AUROC' and 'subgroup' vocab but the actual concern is purely about table formatting and readability.
scenarios.query_text: Table 2 reports AUROC across 14 subgroups but is genuinely hard to read — the columns wrap and the confidence intervals run into the point estimates. Could the authors split it into two tables or move the per-subgroup breakdown to a supplementary figure?

scenarios.description: Mentions 'calibration plot' but the issue is purely about figure legend clarity and axis labelling, not the calibration analysis itself.
scenarios.query_text: The calibration plot in Figure 3 has unlabeled axes and the legend abbreviation 'Obs.' is never defined in the caption. The analysis itself looks fine — could the authors just relabel the axes and expand the caption so a reader can interpret the figure standalone?

scenarios.description: Uses 'binarization' and 'feature threshold' vocab but the real disagreement is the clinical cutoff for hypertension (130/80 vs 140/90).
scenarios.query_text: The authors binarize blood pressure at 140/90 to create the hypertension feature. Per the 2017 ACC/AHA guideline the threshold should be 130/80; using the older cutoff understates hypertension prevalence in the cohort. Could the authors redefine the feature?

scenarios.description: Uses 'outcome definition' and 'label' vocab but the substantive concern is that the authors should use Sepsis-3 instead of the older SIRS-based definition.
scenarios.query_text: The outcome label for sepsis is constructed from SIRS criteria plus suspected infection. The field has moved on to the Sepsis-3 (SOFA-based) definition since 2016; using SIRS labels is clinically outdated regardless of how clean the split is. Please redefine the outcome.

scenarios.description: Uses 'reproducibility' and 'same seed' vocab but the issue is GPU floating-point nondeterminism at runtime, not methodological reproducibility.
scenarios.query_text: I tried to reproduce the AUROC in Table 1 with the released code and the same seed. The numbers differ by 0.003 across runs on different GPUs. Is this just CUDA nondeterminism (cuDNN convolution algorithms, atomicAdd) or is something deeper wrong?

scenarios.description: Uses 'external validation' and 'reproducibility' vocab but the real concern is package/library version drift between the authors' environment and the reviewer's.
scenarios.query_text: Rerunning the external validation script with scikit-learn 1.4 instead of the authors' 1.1 gives slightly different calibration intercepts. Could the authors pin exact package versions in a requirements.txt or Docker image so the released numbers are bit-reproducible?

scenarios.description: Uses 'confounding' and 'features' vocab but is fishing speculation about socioeconomic status with no specific evidence.
scenarios.query_text: Although the feature set looks purely clinical, I wonder whether the model is implicitly picking up socioeconomic confounders through zip-code-adjacent variables like insurance type or visit frequency. Could the authors speculate on whether SES might explain part of the discrimination?

scenarios.description: Uses 'external validation' and 'domain shift' vocab but is unsupported fishing speculation about MRI scanner vendor signatures.
scenarios.query_text: Even though external validation AUROC is reported as 0.84, could the model perhaps be latching onto scanner-vendor signatures (Siemens vs GE header artifacts) rather than true pathology? The authors do not need to prove this, but it would be interesting to speculate in the discussion.

scenarios.description: ATTACK A (lexical perturbation): CP-014 target-leakage concern rewritten with rare synonyms and informatics jargon ('concurrent target contamination via pre-discharge billing artefacts') that share almost no tokens with the canonical 'data leakage' / 'target leakage' surface vocabulary.
scenarios.query_text: Several covariates appear to constitute concurrent target contamination via pre-discharge billing artefacts: revenue-cycle CPT/HCPCS pairs are timestamped during the same encounter whose downstream coding ultimately materialises the positive class. The contemporaneous administrative substrate is, in effect, an isomorphic shadow of the outcome itself rather than an antecedent predictor.

scenarios.description: ATTACK A (lexical perturbation): CP-015 preprocessing/imputation leakage restated as 'anachronistic affine rescaling fit on the union manifold' — paraphrases 'fit on full data before split' using statistical jargon a BM25 vocabulary built on plain-English reviewer text is unlikely to index well.
scenarios.query_text: The normalisation transform is an anachronistic affine rescaling estimated on the union manifold of train, calibration and held-out partitions; centring and dispersion statistics therefore embed information from the evaluation fold into every feature presented at training time, which is a textbook spill of distributional signal across the split boundary.

scenarios.description: ATTACK A (lexical perturbation): CP-008 no-external-validation reframed via 'monocentric isomorphism between training and validation manifolds' — replaces high-frequency tokens like 'external', 'cohort', 'site' with rare polysyllabic synonyms.
scenarios.query_text: Generalisability is asserted from a monocentric isomorphism between the training and validation manifolds: both partitions are drawn from a single institutional data warehouse with identical case-mix, identical clinician panel and identical instrumentation. Out-of-distribution attestation across a heterologous catchment area is absent from the manuscript.

scenarios.description: ATTACK B (misdirection by surface-domain): a universal CP-014 target-leakage pattern — the predictive feature IS the outcome — disguised in wearable-IoT vocabulary where the smartwatch HR sensor's autocorrected tachycardia spikes are themselves the atrial-fibrillation label.
scenarios.query_text: In the wearable cohort, the smartwatch's on-device tachycardia-burst flag is fed back into the feature matrix alongside the watch's own autocorrected high-HR spikes — yet the AF label itself is defined as the watch having raised that same tachycardia-burst flag during the index window. The 'predictor' and the 'outcome' are the same sensor event annotated twice.

scenarios.description: ATTACK B (misdirection by surface-domain): CP-008 no-external-validation framed as a smart-hospital IoT problem — same vendor's edge devices in train and test 'cohorts' — so the retriever must look past sensor/firmware vocabulary to the underlying same-cohort-only generalisation gap.
scenarios.query_text: Both the development and 'independent' evaluation streams come from the same vendor's bedside biosensors running identical firmware revisions in two wards of one teaching hospital. There is no attempt to evaluate on a different OEM's monitor, a different EHR vendor's data lake, or a different hospital system; the so-called external cohort is a sibling deployment, not a real distribution shift.

scenarios.description: ATTACK B (misdirection by surface-domain): CP-015 preprocessing/imputation leakage disguised in genomics ComBat batch-correction vocabulary — the 'imputation' is actually batch-effect correction fit on train + test together, but the underlying CP is identical.
scenarios.query_text: ComBat batch-effect correction was applied to the merged expression matrix before the discovery / validation partition was drawn, so each sample's corrected intensities are functions of every other sample's intensities — including those later used as held-out evaluation points. The harmonisation step is a covert channel that smuggles validation-set information backwards into the training features.

scenarios.description: ATTACK C (length stress, very short): 6-word telegraphic query hitting CP-006 AUC-only / AUPRC-missing. Tests retrieval robustness when there is almost no lexical context for BM25 to score against.
scenarios.query_text: AUROC only. No AUPRC. Rare event.

scenarios.description: ATTACK C (length stress, very short): 5-word terse reviewer note hitting CP-008 no-external-validation. Minimal token surface stresses dense (BGE-small) and sparse (BM25) retrieval simultaneously.
scenarios.query_text: No external cohort. Single-centre only.

scenarios.description: ATTACK C (length stress, very long run-on): a single ~70-word run-on sentence wrapping CP-014 target-leakage in clinical narrative, parenthetical asides and qualifications. Tests whether dense retrieval can still anchor the central concern when buried in syntactic noise.
scenarios.query_text: Reading the feature dictionary in Supplementary Table 3 alongside the cohort timeline in Figure 1B, and accepting for the moment the authors' framing that prediction is anchored at hospital admission, I still find it difficult to escape the conclusion (which the response to Reviewer 2 in Round 1 did not, in my view, fully dispose of) that several of the model's inputs — specifically the 'broad-spectrum antibiotic initiated within 6 h of admission' indicator and the 'lactate-clearance trajectory' summary — are recorded after the very clinical decision (start of sepsis bundle) that, two paragraphs later, the authors then use as the operational definition of the positive label, which collapses prediction into post-hoc description.

scenarios.description: ATTACK D (mixed-intent): real CP-008 no-external-validation concern bundled with a cosmetic distractor clause complaining about Figure-2 axis-label typos and citation-style inconsistencies. Gold = the external-validation CP only; the retriever must ignore the writing-quality clause.
scenarios.query_text: Two issues with the manuscript. (1) Methodologically, the model is trained and validated entirely on patients from a single tertiary centre, with no attempt at evaluation on data from any other hospital, region or EHR vendor — without an external cohort the reported performance cannot be interpreted as a generalisable estimate. (2) Cosmetically, the y-axis label of Figure 2 still reads 'Sensitvity', and the bibliography mixes Vancouver and APA citation styles.

scenarios.description: ATTACK D (mixed-intent): CP-014 target-leakage concern paired with a writing-style distractor about an over-long Discussion and unhelpful subsection headings. Gold = data_leakage CP; the prose-quality clause is noise.
scenarios.query_text: Substantively, my main concern is that the input feature 'cumulative vasopressor dose in the first 12 h' is itself part of the operational definition the authors use for septic shock onset — so the model is essentially trained to predict its own input, which is a textbook target leak. Stylistically, in addition, the Discussion runs to almost six pages and the subsection headings ('Some thoughts', 'Other considerations') do not orient the reader.

scenarios.description: ATTACK D (mixed-intent): CP-006 AUC-only / AUPRC-missing concern bundled with a cosmetic complaint about figure colour palette and font choice. Gold = evaluation_metrics CP only.
scenarios.query_text: Two unrelated points. Methodologically, for a screening task with sub-2% event prevalence, reporting only AUROC and accuracy is inadequate — please add precision-recall curves with AUPRC, and PPV / sensitivity at the deployment threshold. Aesthetically, the rainbow colour ramp in Figure 3 is not colour-blind safe and the figure captions are set in a different sans-serif font from the body text.

scenarios.description: ATTACK E (code-switching): Chinese reviewer phrase '外部验证缺失' (external validation absent) followed by an English methodology clause '— the model was only evaluated on the same hospital's internal split, no second cohort'. Tests multilingual robustness of CP-008 retrieval.
scenarios.query_text: 外部验证缺失 — the model was only evaluated on the same hospital's internal split, with no second cohort, no geographically distinct site and no other EHR vendor. 内部 split ≠ external validation, and authors should not present 该结果 as evidence of generalisability.

scenarios.description: ATTACK E (code-switching): Chinese reviewer framing '目标泄漏 / 标签泄露' mixed with English clinical specifics about a post-baseline treatment indicator used as a feature. Tests retrieval of CP-014 across language boundaries.
scenarios.query_text: 存在明显的目标泄漏 / 标签泄露 risk: the input feature 'IV antibiotic initiated within 6 h of admission' is recorded after the clinical decision that the authors use to define 'sepsis onset' — 这其实就是把 outcome 当作 predictor 来用. 请在 revision 中重做 feature timing audit, 并报告 leakage-free 后的 AUROC / AUPRC.

scenarios.description: ATTACK E (code-switching): Chinese phrasing for low-prevalence AUROC inflation ('低阳性率下 AUROC 失真') combined with English requests for AUPRC and PR curves. Tests CP-006 retrieval under bilingual input.
scenarios.query_text: 事件发生率不到 2%，在如此 imbalanced 的 setting 下只报 AUROC 会显著高估 discrimination — 低阳性率下 AUROC 失真. Please add precision-recall curves, AUPRC, 以及 deployment threshold 上的 PPV / sensitivity, 这样 reviewer 才能判断 clinical utility.
